pullRequests.title: V0: markdown files with front matter, a website, and a command line tool
pullRequests.body:
## What this adds

V0 of Heidrun Notebook, as decided in #2. V0 stores markdown files with front matter. A person sees and searches the files in a website, and manages the files with a command line tool. The five child issues are stacked on top of each other, so this one pull request holds all of them.

- #3 — Setup: the pnpm workspace, the three packages, `.env.example`, `pnpm dev`, and `pnpm test`.
- #4 — Slice 1: create a file with the command line tool, and see the file in the list of the website.
- #5 — Slice 2: read one file in the website and with the command line tool. The website cleans the HTML made from the markdown.
- #6 — Slice 3: search in the website and with the command line tool.
- #7 — Slice 4: update and delete with the command line tool.

Closes #3, closes #4, closes #5, closes #6, closes #7.

## How it was checked

- On a clean clone: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm test` (232 tests), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, and `pnpm typecheck` all succeed.
- The final check of V0 in #2 was done with the real `pnpm dev` and a real browser, with one start of the server:
  - The command line tool created three files. The website listed them, opened each one, and found each one with the search box.
  - After `update` on one file and `delete` on another file, the website showed the new content and no longer showed the deleted file.
- A markdown file with a `<script>` element, an `onerror` attribute, a `javascript:` link, and a form did not run any script in the browser.

## Decisions that the issues did not state

Please confirm or change each one.

- The version of TypeScript is `~6.0.3`, because `vue-tsc` does not support TypeScript 7.
- `pnpm dev` creates `.env` from `.env.example` when `.env` does not exist, because a clean clone has no `.env`.
- The server accepts only paths that end with `.md`. The server refuses a wrong Host header (403), a request body that is not declared as `application/json` (415), and a request body larger than one mebibyte (413). The reason is that V0 has no sign-in, and a web page of another site must not be able to write files.
- `GET /api/files/<path>` answers 422 when the front matter of the file on the disk cannot be read. The list route shows such a file with an empty front matter. #2 lists only 400 and 404 for this route.
- The server does not normalize the URL, so a path with `..` gets the status code 400. The command line tool and the website refuse a path with a `.` or `..` segment before they send a request.
- The search matches a word inside a longer word. A missing or empty query gives an empty list.
- `PUT /api/files/<path>` requires both `frontMatter` and `body`. The command line tool refuses `update` with no content option, because such a call would empty the file. The server writes a hidden temporary file and renames it over the old file.
- Every answer of the server has `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Prettier and ESLint apply the code style. The website tests run in `jsdom`, because DOMPurify does not work in `happy-dom`.

## Not in this pull request

- #8, the SQLite search index, is not part of V0.
- #2 stays open. Its checkboxes are not ticked.
- Markdown tables show without borders in the website. This is only a matter of style.
- After the merge, the branches `v0-setup`, `v0-slice-1`, `v0-slice-2`, `v0-slice-3`, and `v0-slice-4` can be deleted.

pullRequests.title: Product: make project records dependable (Milestone 1)
pullRequests.body:
Project records could previously lose structured metadata or overwrite newer changes, and file writes had no recorded recovery outcome when history failed. This change adds structured field input, revision-checked partial updates and deletions, validated minimum record formats, and grouped writes with persistent retry receipts and a recoverable pending journal.

Each person's content has independent Git history attributed to the authenticated person. The read-only website shows exact edits, pending recording, nested record links, missing targets, and history for deleted records. The notebook skill and concept documents define the matching read, prepare, review, write, verify, and recover procedure.

Validation: all 599 tests passed, including real-process restart recovery, direct-caller revision checks, and user isolation. Type, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. Live tool and Chrome checks demonstrated metadata preservation, stale-update refusal, Git recording failure, a genuinely partial filesystem failure, and recovery. The developer reviewed and accepted the result.

Scope: one writing server process per content folder. Grouped changes are recoverable but not atomically visible. Concurrent manual writes, remote hosting, power-loss durability, and backups are outside the demonstrated local scope.

Closes [Milestone 1](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/49). Part of the [roadmap master issue](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/46). [Live evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/49#issuecomment-6312038845).

pullRequests.title: Share any document with another person and remove the shared summaries
pullRequests.body:
Fixes #108.

Any document can be shared with another person. The recipient reads the shared document itself, with its front matter and its body, as it is at each read. The application has no summary any more: not in the server, not in the website, not in the command line tool `heidrun_notebook_ctrl`, not in the skills, and not in the documents.

- A share has a document path, a recipient email address, and a duration. It has no title, no summary text, and no source revision.
- The owner approval on `/access` and the revocation stay.
- The recipient gets the file name, the front matter and the body, and never the path of the document in the notebook of the owner.
- A shared document that the owner deleted is unavailable to the recipient.
- The recipient reads the current document at each read, so a later change by the owner is visible to the recipient.

The files [authentication_routes.ts](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/packages/web_server/src/http/authentication_routes.ts) and [user_store.ts](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/packages/web_server/src/authentication/user_store.ts) need no change: they only check that the recipient account exists. issues.title: V0 roadmap
issues.body:
## Goal of V0

V0 is the first implementation of Heidrun Notebook. V0 does one thing: it stores markdown files with front matter. A person can see these files in a web browser, search them, and manage them with a command line tool. This follows the conclusions of issue #1. This issue is the parent issue: it holds the decisions and the contract of V0, and each child issue holds the tasks of one slice.

## Product decisions

- V0 has no sign-in. The server reads one username from the variable `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_USERNAME` in the `.env` file, and V0 serves only that username.
- The server only accepts connections from the same computer, because V0 has no sign-in.
- The website is read-only in V0. The person writes, updates, and deletes with the command line tool only. The website only shows and searches.
- The markdown files are stored as raw files on the disk, in the folder `./content/<username>/`. `<username>` is the name of the user. Inside this folder, the files follow a relative folder hierarchy, and the person chooses the folders.
- Every markdown file contains front matter. The front matter holds the metadata about the content of the file, so the metadata travels inside the file itself. No separate file and no database holds metadata. A program can read the front matter to classify, filter, and search the files.
- No front matter field is required in V0. The website shows every field it finds. Required fields can be added later, when the need is clear.
- A database is not the source of truth. The markdown files are the source of truth. If the search is too slow, a SQLite search index can be added later, see the last issue of the roadmap.

## Technology decisions

- The frontend uses Vue.
- The style uses Bootstrap 6, pinned to the exact version `6.0.0-alpha.1`. Bootstrap 6 is a pre-release version today, and the decision is to use Bootstrap 6 anyway.
- The server uses Node.
- The package manager is pnpm.
- The repository is a monorepo, which means one repository that holds three packages. The packages are linked with pnpm workspaces:
  - `packages/server` — the Node server and its application programming interface.
  - `packages/frontend` — the Vue website.
  - `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl` — the command line tool. The command line tool talks directly to the application programming interface of the server.
- All configuration is in a `.env` file, as environment variables. The `.env` file is not committed to git. The repository holds a `.env.example` file that lists every variable.
- The website cleans the HTML made from the markdown before the browser shows the HTML.
- Every slice has automated tests. The test runner is Vitest, for the server, the Vue website, and the command line tool. One command, `pnpm test`, runs all of the tests.

## Out of scope for V0

- Many users, accounts, sign-in, and permissions.
- Sharing notes with clients.
- Artificial intelligence features (summaries, extraction, recaps).
- Project management, decision logs, and links to issues.
- A local desktop application.

## Application programming interface routes

The paths in the routes are relative to the folder `./content/<username>/`. Every route answers in JavaScript Object Notation. An error answer has a status code and a field `error` that holds a clear message.

| Action | Route | Meaning | Error status codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create | `POST /api/files` | The request holds `path`, `frontMatter`, and `body`. Answers with the status code 201. | 400 for a path that leaves the folder or a front matter that cannot be read, 409 when the file exists |
| List | `GET /api/files` | Answers with the `path` and the `frontMatter` of every file. | none |
| Read | `GET /api/files/<path>` | Answers with `path`, `frontMatter`, and `body`. | 400 for a path that leaves the folder, 404 when the file does not exist |
| Update | `PUT /api/files/<path>` | Replaces the whole file. The update does not merge front matter fields. | 400, 404 |
| Delete | `DELETE /api/files/<path>` | Deletes the file. Answers with the status code 204. | 400, 404 |
| Search | `GET /api/search?query=<words>` | Answers with the same fields as the list route. | none |

## Roadmap

Each line is one child issue. The child issues are done in this order. Each slice works from end to end, so a person can try V0 after each slice.

- [x] #3 — V0 setup: the repository, the three packages, the `.env.example` file, `pnpm dev`, and `pnpm test`.
- [x] #4 — Slice 1: create a file with the command line tool and see the file in the website list.
- [x] #5 — Slice 2: read one file, in the website and with the command line tool.
- [x] #6 — Slice 3: search, in the website and with the command line tool.
- [x] #7 — Slice 4: update and delete, with the command line tool.
- [ ] #8 — After V0: the SQLite search index, only if the search is too slow. This issue is not part of V0.

## Final check of V0

- [x] With the command line tool, create three markdown files that have front matter.
- [x] In the web browser, see the three files in the list, open each file, and find each file with the search box.
- [x] With the command line tool, delete one file, and see that the web browser no longer shows the file.

issues.title: Multi-user slice 3 — Each person sees only the files of that person
issues.body:
Part of the multi-user work. Do this issue after #11 (sign in). Each person of the authentication fixture sees only the files of that person: Alice sees only the files of Alice, Bob sees only the files of Bob, and Carol sees only the files of Carol. A person who is not signed in sees no file.

## The rule

| Name | Email address | Folder of the files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alice Example | `alice@example.com` | `content/alice/` |
| Bob Example | `bob@example.com` | `content/bob/` |
| Carol Example | `carol@example.com` | `content/carol/` |

- The server takes the folder from the session of the request. The folder never comes from the request, so a person cannot name the folder of another person.
- A request for a file of another person gets the status code 404. This is the same answer as for a file that does not exist, so the answer does not tell that the file exists.
- A path that starts with `bob/`, sent by Alice, is a subfolder named `bob` inside the folder of Alice. It is not the folder of Bob.
- The existing files of Alice stay where they are, in `content/alice/`.

## Risk to test first

The assumption that could make this issue impossible: the command line tool can sign in and send the session cookie back. The routes of the files need a session after this issue, and Node does not keep cookies by itself. Before any other task, test this against the real server, with no mock:

- [ ] With `fetch` in Node, send `POST /api/auth/sign_in`, read the `Set-Cookie` header of the answer, send the value in the `Cookie` header of `GET /api/files`, and check that the answer is not 401. Write the raw output in this issue.

## Decision to confirm before the work starts

The routes under `/api/files` and `/api/search` need a session after this issue, so the command line tool must sign in too. Proposal: the command line tool reads the variables `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_EMAIL` and `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` from the `.env` file, signs in at the start of each command, and works only on the files of that person. If another way is better, for example a route without a session that accepts connections from the same computer only, say so in this issue. That would let any program on the computer read every file, so the rule above would not hold for it.

## Tasks

### Server

- [ ] Add the name of the folder to each user of the authentication fixture: `alice`, `bob`, and `carol`.
- [ ] Keep the folder name in the session. The answers of `POST /api/auth/sign_in` and `GET /api/auth/me` do not change.
- [ ] Answer every route under `/api/files` and `/api/search` with the status code 401 when nobody is signed in.
- [ ] Make every route under `/api/files` and `/api/search` work in the folder of the signed in person only: create, read, update, delete, list, and search.
- [ ] Remove the variable `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_USERNAME` from the server configuration and from `.env.example`, because the server no longer has one user.
- [ ] A person whose folder does not exist yet gets an empty list, and the first create makes the folder.

### Command line tool

- [ ] Add the variables `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_EMAIL` and `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` to the configuration and to `.env.example`.
- [ ] Sign in at the start of each command, and send the session cookie with every request of the command. A wrong sign in prints `error: <message>` on the standard error output and ends with the exit code 1.
- [ ] Update the skill `heidrun_notebook_ctrl`: the two variables, and the error of a wrong sign in. The test `skill_documentation.test.ts` must still pass.

### Website

- [ ] The pages `/documents` and `/files/<path>` send a person who is not signed in to `/sign_in`.
- [ ] The page of one file of another person shows the same error as a file that does not exist.

### Tests

- [ ] Test the server for each of the three persons: the list holds only the files of that person, the read of an own file works, and the read, the update, and the delete of a file of each of the two other persons give 404 and change nothing.
- [ ] Test that the search finds only the files of the signed in person, with a word that is in the files of all three persons.
- [ ] Test that a create writes into the folder of the signed in person, and that a path that starts with `bob/`, sent by Alice, stays in the folder of Alice.
- [ ] Test that every route under `/api/files` and `/api/search` gives 401 without a session.
- [ ] Test that two persons signed in at the same time do not see the files of each other.
- [ ] Test the command line tool against the real server: a good sign in, a wrong password, and that each command works on the files of the person of the variables only.
- [ ] Test the website pages: signed out, and signed in as each of the three persons.
- [ ] Test in a real browser, and write the raw output in this issue: sign in as Alice and see only the files of Alice. Sign out, sign in as Bob, and see only the files of Bob. Do the same for Carol. As Bob, type the address of a file of Alice, and see the error "does not exist".

### Documents

- [ ] Update the `CONTEXT.md` files of the server, of the website, and of the command line tool. These rules change: "the server serves the files of one user named in `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_USERNAME`", "the routes under `/api/files` and `/api/search` stay without authentication", and "the command line tool needs no sign in".
- [ ] Update `README.md` with the new variables and the folder of each person.

## Out of scope

- Sharing a file with another person, and any permission other than "only the owner".
- A person who sees all files.
- Real accounts, registration, and hashing of passwords. See #11.
- Moving a file from one person to another.
- Protection of the files on the disk: any program of the computer can still read the folder `content/`.

## Done when

A person signs in as `alice@example.com` and sees only the files in `content/alice/`. The person signs out, signs in as `bob@example.com`, and sees only the files in `content/bob/`. Carol sees only the files in `content/carol/`. The address of a file of Alice, typed while signed in as Bob, shows "does not exist". The command line tool, with the email address and the password of Bob, lists only the files of Bob.

issues.title: Add an end-to-end test layer in each package
issues.body:
Add an end-to-end test layer in each package: `packages/server`, `packages/frontend`, and `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl`. An end-to-end test uses the real parts of the product, with no fake in place of another package.

Today each package has Vitest test files next to the source files, and these tests do not use the real parts of the product in the same way:

- `packages/server`: the tests start the server application inside the test process (`server_application.test.ts`). No test starts the server as its own process, the way `pnpm start` starts it.
- `packages/frontend`: the tests answer every request with `FakeServer` (`src/fake_server.ts`). No test runs the website against the real server, so a change in the application programming interface of the server that the fake server does not copy is not found.
- `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl`: the tests already start the real server in its own process (`RunningTestServer`, `src/running_test_server.ts`). This is the model for the other two packages.

Scope:

- Each package gets one end-to-end test layer, run with its own command, for example `pnpm --filter <package name> test:end_to_end`.
- The server layer starts the real server process with an empty content folder in a temporary folder, and sends real requests for sign in, create, list, read, search, update, delete, and sign out.
- The frontend layer runs the website against the real server process, and checks sign in, the file list, one file, and search in a real browser page.
- The command line tool layer keeps `RunningTestServer`, and checks every command against the real server.
- Each layer checks that one person sees only the files of that person, with Alice Example and Bob Example from the authentication fixture of the server.
- The command `pnpm test` at the root runs the end-to-end layer of every package, or the issue says why it does not.
- A package imports another package only through the `exports` entry of that package. An end-to-end test starts the server as a process, so no package imports the code of the server package.
- Each `CONTEXT.md` file of the three packages names the command of its end-to-end layer.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each of the three packages has an end-to-end test layer with its own command.
- Each layer passes on a clean checkout after `pnpm install`, with no running server and no `.env` file other than the one that `pnpm dev` creates.
- Each layer uses a free port and a temporary content folder, so it does not touch the `content/` folder and it does not stop a running `pnpm dev`.
- The raw output of each layer, from a real run, is in a comment of this issue.
- `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass at the root.

- Each command sends two more requests to the server (the sign in and the sign out), and makes a new session each time.

1. How does the tool get its credentials: the variables in `.env` as today, a `sign_in` command that keeps the session in a file, or one token for each person?
2. Does the tool ask for the password in the terminal, so that no file holds the password?
3. How does a person choose another person for one command, without editing the file `.env`?
4. Do the sessions need an expiry time, so that a session kept in a file does not stay valid forever?

## Done when

To be written after the questions above have an answer.

Add a `README.md` file in each package of the repository, so that a person who opens a package folder on GitHub or in an editor learns what the package is and how to use it, without the need to read the `README.md` file at the root.

The repository has three packages, and none has a `README.md` file today:

- `packages/server`
- `packages/frontend`
- `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl`

A `README.md` file is for a person who uses or runs the package. It is not a copy of the `CONTEXT.md` file, which is for a coding agent and lists the rules and the boundaries of the folder. Each `README.md` file links to the `CONTEXT.md` file and to the `README.md` file at the root, and does not copy a fact that lives there.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each of the three packages has a `README.md` file.
- Each `README.md` file says what the package does, how to install and run it, how to run its tests, and which environment variables it reads.
- The `README.md` file of `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl` lists the commands of the command line tool and links to its skill.
- Every command written in a `README.md` file was run once and works.
- Each `README.md` file has no sentence that disagrees with the `README.md` file at the root or with the `CONTEXT.md` file of the package.
- The `CONTEXT.md` file of each package, and the `CONTEXT.md` file at the root, name the new `README.md` file.

issues.title: Support Google authentication
issues.body:
Let a person sign in to the website with a Google account, next to the sign in with an email address and a password from the authentication fixture.

## Today

The server knows only three users, Alice Example, Bob Example, and Carol Example, in the authentication fixture `packages/server/src/authentication_fixture.ts`. The fixture is for development and testing only, and its passwords are in clear text ([issue #11](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/11)). The routes `POST /api/auth/sign_in`, `GET /api/auth/me`, and `POST /api/auth/sign_out` start and end a session in the memory of the server. Each user has a fixed folder name, and each person sees only the files in the own folder ([issue #17](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/17)). The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, because the password goes in clear text over HTTP.

## Problems

- A person who is not in the fixture cannot sign in.
- The passwords are in clear text, in the source code and in the `README.md` file.
- Nobody can create a new user without a change to the source code.

## Decisions

1. The Google sign in works next to the fixture. The fixture stays for development and for the tests.
2. The server does the Open Authorization 2.0 authorization code flow and keeps the client secret. The browser never sees the secret. The result is the same cookie session as today, with the cookie `heidrun_notebook_session`.
3. The folder name of a Google account is the stable subject identifier of Google, because the email address of an account can change.
4. Only the email addresses in a list in `.env` may sign in. The list can map an email address to an existing folder name, for example `alice@example.com=alice`. An address with no folder name in the list gets a new folder named after its subject identifier, and the server creates the empty folder on the first sign in.
5. Google sends the person back to `http://localhost:5173/api/auth/google/callback`, through the development server of the website. The website is the address that the person sees.
6. The scope is localhost only. The server keeps listening on `127.0.0.1` only. A public deployment, with a real domain name, HTTPS, and a secure cookie, gets its own issue.
7. The command line tool `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` does not sign in with Google in this issue. It keeps the fixture sign in, and [issue #23](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/23) decides how the tool authenticates.
8. The sessions stay in the memory of the server, as today. A restart signs everyone out.
9. The sign out ends the session of the server only. The Google session of the browser stays.
10. The tests are automatic tests with a fake Google server, plus one manual run with a real Google account, recorded in a comment of this issue.

## First proof

Before the code, prove the one assumption that would make this issue impossible: that Google accepts `http://localhost:5173/api/auth/google/callback` as redirect address, and that the browser keeps the cookie `heidrun_notebook_session` through the development server of the website. Run the proof against the real Google and the real development server, with a real Google account, and record the raw result in a comment of this issue. The proof uses the Google client of the project teamwright, so the developer adds the redirect address to that client in the Google Cloud console by hand. Do not build the rest before the proof works.

## Done when

- The server has the routes `GET /api/auth/google/sign_in`, which sends the person to Google, and `GET /api/auth/google/callback`, which receives the answer of Google. The existing routes of the fixture sign in, `GET /api/auth/me`, and `POST /api/auth/sign_out` keep their behavior.
- The server sends a random state value to Google, keeps it in a short cookie, and refuses the callback when the state value does not match, so that a web page of another site cannot start a sign in.
- The server accepts the answer of Google only when the identity token has the right issuer, the right audience (the client identifier of this server), a time that has not passed, and an email address that Google marks as verified.
- A Google account whose email address is not in the list gets no session. The sign in page shows a clear message, and the server makes no folder.
- A Google account whose email address is in the list gets a new session and the cookie `heidrun_notebook_session`, as the fixture sign in does. A sign in always starts a new session and ends the session of the request.
- The folder of the person is the folder named in the list, or the subject identifier of Google when the list names none. The server creates the folder when it does not exist. A person sees only the files in the own folder, as in [issue #17](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/17).
- The server reads three environment variables from `.env`, and `.env.example` lists them with a comment each and no value: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_GOOGLE_ALLOWED_EMAILS` (the list of email addresses, with the optional folder names). The first two have the same names as in the project teamwright. The two must both be set or both be left out, and the server refuses to start when only one is set. The values of the client identifier and of the client secret are never written in a log, in an issue, in a comment, in a commit, or in a pull request.
- When `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is not set, the Google routes answer with the status code 404, and the sign in page shows no Google button. The website learns this from the server.
- The sign in page of the website has a "Sign in with Google" button next to the form of the fixture.
- Automatic tests with a fake Google server cover the list of tests below. `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm format:check` pass.
- One manual run with a real Google account, from the first click to the list of files, is recorded in a comment of this issue, with the raw output and the date.
- The `README.md` file at the root explains how to create the Google client (the redirect address above, and the three variables, without any value), and the `CONTEXT.md` files of the server and of its `src/` folder describe the new routes and rules.

### Tests to write

- The callback with a wrong state value is refused.
- The callback with an identity token of the wrong issuer, of the wrong audience, that has expired, or with an email address that is not verified is refused.
- An email address not in the list gets no session and no folder.
- An email address in the list with a folder name opens that folder, and its files are the files of that folder only.
- An email address in the list with no folder name gets a folder named after the subject identifier, and the folder is created once.
- The fixture sign in still works when the Google sign in is on, and when it is off.

issues.title: Move every test of a package into the folder test of that package
issues.body:
## Problem

The tests of each package are in two places, and they have no common folder:

- The unit tests are in `src`, next to the file they test. For example `packages/frontend/src` holds 10 files `*.test.ts`, `packages/server/src` holds 13, and `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/src` holds 2.
- The end-to-end tests are in the folder `end_to_end` at the root of each package, with the file `vitest.end_to_end.config.ts` beside it.
- The helpers that only tests use are mixed with the source code. For example `packages/frontend/src/fake_server.ts`.

A reader cannot find all the tests of a package in one place, and `src` holds code that is not part of the product.

## Wanted

Each package has one folder `test`, and every test of the package is inside it. No test and no test helper stays in `src`. For example, for the website: `packages/frontend/test`. The same for `packages/server` and `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl`.

Inside the folder `test`, the end-to-end tests and the other tests are in their own subfolders.

## Proposal

```
packages/<package>/
  src/                 source code only
  test/
    unit/              the tests that are in src today, and their helpers
    end_to_end/        the tests that are in end_to_end today, and their helpers
```

## What must change with the move

- Move the files `*.test.ts` out of `src`, and fix their imports of the source files.
- Move the test helpers out of `src`: `packages/frontend/src/fake_server.ts` is the known one. Look for others.
- Move the folder `end_to_end` of each package into `test`.
- Update the settings of Vitest and of TypeScript, so that `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm lint` find the tests in the new place.
- Add a file `CONTEXT.md` to each new folder, and update the existing ones. The rule "Tests sit next to the file they test" in the files `CONTEXT.md` of `src` must change.
- Update `README.md` when it names a test path.

## Questions to decide

1. Are the names of the two subfolders `unit` and `end_to_end`?
2. Where do the files `vitest.end_to_end.config.ts` go: in `test`, or at the root of the package?
3. Do the tests keep the suffix `.test.ts`?

## Related

- The renaming of the folders of the two packages is in issue 27. The paths of this issue use the names of today. Do one issue first, and update the other:
- https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/27

## Done when

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm format:check` pass.
- No file `*.test.ts` and no test helper is in `src` of any package.
- Each package has the folder `test` with its own file `CONTEXT.md`.

issues.title: Run the command line tool heidrun_notebook_ctrl with npx, without the script start
issues.body:
## Problem

The file `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/package.json` has a script named `start`. Every example in the documentation runs the command line tool through this script, for example `pnpm --filter heidrun_notebook_ctrl start login`. The command is long. The word `start` also suggests a server that keeps running, but the command line tool runs one command and exits.

## Wanted

A person runs the command line tool by its own name with `npx`, from the root folder of the repository, with no `pnpm --filter` and no `start`:

```
npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl login
npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl list
npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl read notes/welcome.md
```

Publishing the package on npmjs, so that the same command works on any computer, is a separate issue.

## Tasks

- Remove the script `start` from `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/package.json`.
- Add a `bin` entry named `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` in the same file, pointing to `src/main.ts`, so that the command `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` exists.
- Add `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` with the version `workspace:*` to the `devDependencies` of the root `package.json`, so that `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl` finds the command in the root folder.
- Keep the loading of the `.env` file at the root of the repository. The script `start` loads it today with `--env-file-if-exists=../../.env`.
- Replace every `pnpm --filter heidrun_notebook_ctrl start` (and `pnpm --silent --filter heidrun_notebook_ctrl start`) with `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl` in these files:
  - `README.md`
  - `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/README.md`
  - `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/CONTEXT.md`
  - `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/skills/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/SKILL.md`
  - `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/test/unit/skill_documentation.test.ts`
- Replace the sentence "The `pnpm start` command reads the `.env` file at the root" in `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/README.md` with a sentence that is true for the new command.

## Done when

- `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl --help` works from the root folder of the repository after `pnpm install`.
- `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl login` signs in, as the script `start` does today.
- A search for `heidrun_notebook_ctrl start` in the repository finds nothing.
- The unit tests and the end to end tests pass.

issues.title: Publish the command line tool heidrun_notebook_ctrl on npmjs
issues.body:
## Problem

The package `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` is private and its entry file is TypeScript, so a person can run the command line tool only inside a checkout of this repository. A person on another computer cannot run `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl login`.

## Wanted

After the package is published on npmjs, this command works on any computer that has Node.js:

```
npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl login
```

The name `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` is free on npmjs today: `npm view heidrun_notebook_ctrl` answers with the error 404.

This issue depends on the issue #34, which adds the `bin` entry and the command `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl` inside the repository.

## Tasks

- Remove `"private": true` from `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/package.json` and set a real version instead of `0.0.0`.
- Add a build step that compiles the TypeScript of the package into JavaScript in a folder named `dist`.
- Point the `bin` entry to the compiled file `dist/main.js`, and write the line `#!/usr/bin/env node` at the top of that file.
- Add a `files` field so that the published package holds the folder `dist`, the `README.md`, and nothing else.
- Move the packages that the compiled code needs at run time (`commander`, `yaml`, `zod`) into `dependencies`, and keep `tsx` out of the run time path.
- Decide where the published tool reads `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_SERVER_ADDRESS` and `HEIDRUN_NOTEBOOK_WEBSITE_ADDRESS`. Today the script `start` reads them from the `.env` file at the root of the repository, and a person on another computer has no such file. The options are:
  - a default address;
  - the environment variables of the terminal only;
  - a configuration file next to the credential file.
- Write in `packages/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/README.md` how a person installs and runs the published tool.
- Add a test that runs `npm pack` and then runs the packed tool with `--help`.

## Done when

- `npm publish` succeeds for the package `heidrun_notebook_ctrl`.
- In a new empty folder outside this repository, `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl --help` prints the help text.
- In the same folder, `npx heidrun_notebook_ctrl login` signs in against a running server.

issues.title: Product: deliver the project management roadmap
issues.body:
## Purpose

Track delivery of the project management workflow described in [docs/roadmap.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md): a person works with a coding agent to understand a project, review proposals, perform authorised work, and maintain project records; Heidrun Notebook stores the records and presents useful views.

This issue tracks delivery. [Product: brainstorm the purpose and proposed roadmap](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/40) remains the related product discussion. All seven milestones (0–6) are implemented, accepted by the developer, merged, and closed as completed. All linked implementation sub-issues are closed. Completion covers the agreed local pilot; remote service readiness remains outside this delivered scope.

## Testing clarification agreed on 21 October 2026

Any coding agent compatible with `SKILL.md` can read and follow the notebook skills and test the workflow itself. Heidrun Code is not a prerequisite for the general feasibility check or subsequent workflow validation. A Heidrun Code session is needed only for claims specific to the Heidrun Code application.

Checks must still use the real `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` command line tool, running service, and website where relevant. Direct edits to the content folder or mocked services do not prove the supported connection works. The roadmap was aligned with this clarification as part of Milestone 0.

## Milestones

- [x] **[Milestone 0 — Prove the working connection (proof of feasibility)](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/47).** Follow the existing skill with a compatible coding agent. In a designated populated test project, read an existing record, create a related note with Unicode, multiline content and links, read the note back, and inspect the note in the website. Exercise supported login approval when required. Test structured metadata separately and retain raw output, browser observations, and precise limitations. A successful basic note does not prove richer project records work.
- [x] **[Milestone 1 — Make project records dependable](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/49).** Agree the minimum customer, project, meeting, decision and task definitions. Preserve structured and unknown fields, validate records and links, protect against older updates overwriting newer changes, define retries and partial failure recovery, and provide usable change history. Update the tool skill alongside the supported commands. Demonstrate representative failures and recovery through the public tool and website.
- [x] **[Milestone 2 — Deliver the first useful project workflow](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/50).** Set up a project, process a supplied meeting transcript, review proposals, and inspect accepted changes in a project view. Preserve the transcript, distinguish recorded human choices from AI recommendations and unresolved requests, link tasks and decisions to sources, and avoid duplicate tasks or unapproved commitments when processing the transcript again.
- [x] **[Milestone 3 — Plan, execute, and review work](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/51).** Support responsibilities, dates, dependencies, blockers, work lists, calendar views, progress reviews, and completion evidence. Demonstrate a revised commitment, an undated task, a dependency, a blocker, and a completed task with evidence, including one authorised piece of project work.
- [x] **[Milestone 4 — Manage changes and complete delivery](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/52).** Handle risks, observed problems, change requests, replaced decisions, deliverables, acceptance, handover, and closure. Prove the selected artifact formats with representative files. Demonstrate corrections, explicit customer acceptance, and remaining obligations without losing earlier decisions.
- [x] **[Milestone 5 — Extend permissions and sharing](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/53).** Define and enforce reusable permissions, scope, duration, revocation, and selected read-only sharing. Verify permitted and refused operations even when a caller ignores skill instructions. Verify restricted information cannot leak through summaries. If a remote pilot is selected, prove authentication, hosting, storage, backups, restoration, and isolation in the intended environment before claiming readiness.
- [x] **[Milestone 6 — Oversee several projects](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/54).** Present commitments, blockers, required decisions, and shared responsibilities across accessible projects. Demonstrate two populated projects with overlapping commitments, a shared contributor, a cross-project dependency, and inaccessible information; obtain the separate authorisations for changes and prevent restricted information from leaking.

## Sequence and dependencies

Milestone 0 precedes Milestone 1; Milestone 1 precedes Milestone 2; Milestone 2 precedes Milestone 3; Milestone 3 precedes Milestone 4. Milestone 5 depends on the relevant workflows from Milestones 2–4. Milestone 6 depends on stable records and access rules from the earlier milestones.

Milestones 0–2 form the first usable local version. Milestones 3–4 establish the broader project management lifecycle. Milestones 5–6 extend permissions, sharing, and oversight across projects. Small parts of later work may be brought forward for the selected pilot, with the resulting scope recorded explicitly.

## Sub-issue organisation

All seven milestones have linked sub-issues. As each milestone becomes actionable, split larger milestones into small implementation tasks that identify:

- The intended person-visible result and dependencies.
- The required notebook change, skill change, and shared record or permission decisions.
- A representative completion scenario and failure cases.
- The person responsible before estimating delivery dates.

Link each sub-issue here and add evidence when marking a milestone complete. Avoid treating a completed website view, written skill, or successful command alone as a complete workflow.

## Completion rules

Each milestone requires the software, skills, and shared definitions needed for the whole intended workflow. Software must enforce the access and operation restrictions that require enforcement. Initially, review proposed changes in the coding agent conversation; do not describe a broad login token as enforcement of individual approvals.

Use the repository's relevant automated checks and real workflow checks. Before building on an unproven external dependency or runtime assumption, name the critical assumption and perform the smallest representative live test. Preserve raw results and state what was actually tested.

Optional connectors, automatic transcription, interactive HTML artifacts, comprehensive financial planning, and additional project management methods remain future choices.

## Milestone 0 completion

Accepted by the developer on 21 October 2026 and merged in [the Milestone 0 pull request](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/pull/48). [Live evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/47#issuecomment-6310569563) demonstrates the basic local connection. Structured list and null metadata remain unsupported and are explicit Milestone 1 work.

## Milestone 1 completion

Accepted by the developer on 21 October 2026 and merged in [the Milestone 1 pull request](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/pull/55). [The implementation evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/milestone_01_evidence.md) records 599 passing tests and real local tool, server, website, failure, and recovery checks. Structured metadata is now supported. Local operation limits remain explicit in the recording contract.

## Roadmap completion — 21 October 2026

Verified all seven linked milestones have state completed, with no open implementation sub-issues. The developer accepted each implementation before its merge. Retained evidence:

| Milestone | Accepted evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Milestone 0 | [Workflow evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/milestone_00_evidence.md) |
| Milestone 1 | [Workflow evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/milestone_01_evidence.md) |

| Milestone 4 | [Workflow evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/milestone_04_evidence.md) |

| Milestone 6 | [Workflow evidence](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/milestone_06_evidence.md) |

The final [Milestone 6 pull request](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/pull/72) is merged. The final full validation passed 658 tests, alongside type checking, lint, formatting and website build. Evidence includes real tool/service/browser checks and independent skill trials, with the tested boundaries and limitations recorded.

This closes delivery of the local roadmap. Development authentication, in-memory permissions/shares and the stated local-operation limitations remain explicit. Remote hosting/authentication, durable remote sharing, remote backup/restoration, optional connectors and other deferred product choices are not claimed as completed by this issue.

issues.title: Product: prove the notebook workflow connection (Milestone 0)
issues.body:
## Purpose

Prove that a coding agent compatible with `SKILL.md` can follow the existing notebook skill, authenticate through the supported human approval process, and read and write representative information through the real `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` command line tool and running notebook service. Inspect the resulting records in the actual website.

Parent: [Product: deliver the project management roadmap](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/46).

Reference: [Milestone 0 in docs/roadmap.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md#milestone-0--prove-the-working-connection).

## Critical assumption

The existing skill and supported tool provide a working connection from a compatible coding agent to the real notebook service. Heidrun Code is not required for this general check: the coding agent performing the work can read and follow `SKILL.md` itself. A separate Heidrun Code check is required only for claims specific to the Heidrun Code application.

## Work

- [ ] Align the roadmap's general testing requirements with the agreed coding-agent compatibility clarification.
- [ ] Read the existing `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` skill and identify the supported installation, command invocation, authentication, and error reporting. Record the actual environment and versions used.
- [ ] Select a designated test project containing representative existing information. If no suitable test project exists, populate a designated test project through supported notebook commands before the scenario. Keep unrelated user records intact.
- [ ] Exercise the supported login approval process when required. Record whether an existing session was reused or a new login was exercised. The person performs any required approval; do not substitute development authentication shortcuts for a claim about the approval process.
- [ ] Read an existing record through `heidrun_notebook_ctrl`.
- [ ] Create a related Markdown note through the tool with accented characters or other Unicode, several lines, and links to existing notebook records.
- [ ] Read the new note back through the tool and compare the saved content with the supplied content.

issues.title: Add a data fixture of notebook files, used by the development application and by the tests
issues.body:
## Problem

- Git ignores the folder `content/`. A clean clone, and every temporary worktree, runs `pnpm dev` with an empty website. The developer must create files by hand before any view shows something.
- Each test writes its own small set of records inside the test code. The test `packages/web_frontend/test/end_to_end/project_workflow.test.ts` writes 17 records. Other tests write other records. The same shapes of customer, project, task, and delivery are written again in many tests, and no test runs against a realistic notebook.
- The files in the local `content/` folder are old samples: recipes, meetings, and one idea. They hold no customer, no project, no task, and no delivery.

## Goal

One data fixture: a set of markdown files, committed to Git, that forms a rich and realistic notebook for the three people of the authentication fixture (Alice Example, Bob Example, and Carol Example). The development application starts from a copy of the data fixture. The tests start from a copy of the data fixture. Nothing writes into the data fixture itself: not the server, not the command line tool, not a test.

## What the data fixture holds

The data fixture is not the minimum. Each record type has several records, and each state that the validators accept appears at least once. All names are made up, all email addresses end with `example.com`, and all dates are fixed dates between September and November 2026.

**Alice Example** has the largest notebook, as a coordinator of several customers:

- Customers in different situations: one with active projects, one whose project is closed after an accepted delivery, and one whose project is cancelled.
- Projects with subprojects, and one subproject with a further subproject. Tasks in two different projects that depend on each other, for the view Across projects. Records of type `availability`, proposed and confirmed.
- Tasks in every status: `proposed`, `rejected`, `planned`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `done` with reported completion, `done` with verified completion, and `cancelled`. Accepted and proposed assignments. Dates that are late, upcoming, and absent. A task that waits for a prerequisite, and a task whose prerequisite link is missing. Progress reports that are recent and progress reports that are old.
- Decisions in every status: `proposed`, `accepted`, `rejected`, and `superseded`, with the pair of links `supersedes` and `superseded_by`.
- Questions that are `open`, `resolved`, and `deferred`.
- Meetings with notes and a transcript, meetings with notes only, and one meeting about several projects.
- Artifacts and source records that other records link to.
- Concerns of kind `risk` and of kind `problem`, in every status: `open`, `responding`, `resolved`, and `accepted_risk`.
- Change requests that are `proposed`, `accepted` (with the linked decision), `rejected`, and `deferred`.
- Deliveries that are `draft`, `in_review`, `corrections_requested`, `accepted` (with the correct revision of every artifact), and `rejected`.
- Closures with the outcomes `closed`, `cancelled`, and `reopened`.
- Personal files outside any customer: notes, recipes, ideas, and a welcome file, so that "My documents" and the search have something to show.
- Files for the markdown reader: a long body, a table, a code block, links between records, and non-Latin characters. Also a few records with optional fields left out, and one older note without a `type`.

**Bob Example** has a smaller notebook, as a contributor: one customer, one project, and a few tasks. Some paths are the same as in the notebook of Alice, with different content, so that the tests can prove that the two notebooks stay separate.

**Carol Example** has only a few personal files and no customer, so that every view shows its empty state.

Rules for every file:

- Every file passes the validators of the server.
- Every relative link resolves, except the missing links that the `CONTEXT.md` of the data fixture names on purpose.
- The field `artifact_revisions` of every accepted delivery holds the SHA-256 hash of the current text of each artifact.
- The folder `.search_index/` is not part of the data fixture. The server builds the search index.

## How the development application uses the data fixture

- Git ignores `content/`, and the developer may keep own files there. So `pnpm dev` never writes over existing files. When `content/` does not exist or holds no file, `pnpm dev` copies the data fixture into `content/` first. This is the way `scripts/ensure_env_file.ts` creates `.env` when `.env` does not exist.
- A second command deletes `content/` and copies the data fixture again, so that the developer can return to the known state after trying the command line tool. The command shows what it deletes and asks for confirmation.
- A temporary worktree has no `content/` folder, because Git ignores it. The copy at the start of `pnpm dev` gives every worktree the same notebook.
- The server keeps the permissions and the shares in memory, and loses them at each restart ([README.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/README.md)). So the data fixture holds files only, and the page "Permissions and sharing" starts empty.

## How the tests use the data fixture

- The class `RunningTestServer` exists in each of the three packages. Each copy copies the data fixture into its temporary content folder when it starts. The copy reads a folder by its path. It imports no code from another package.
- A test that changes files works on the temporary copy, and never on the data fixture.
- A test that now writes many records inline for a normal project reads the data fixture instead. These are, at least, the end-to-end tests `project_workflow`, `oversight_workflow`, `customer_navigation`, `access_workflow`, and `website` of the website package, and the end-to-end test `heidrun_notebook_ctrl` of the command line tool package. The developer who fixes the issue checks the other end-to-end tests of the three packages in the same way.
- A test that needs a record that the data fixture cannot hold still writes the record inline. Examples: an invalid record, and a record that the test itself creates or deletes.
- The unit tests of the validators and of the catalogs of the website read the files of the data fixture instead of long strings in the test code.

## Proposed place

A new folder `data_fixture/` at the root of the repository, with one folder for each person: `data_fixture/alice/`, `data_fixture/bob/`, and `data_fixture/carol/`. The layout inside each folder is the layout of `content/<folder name>/`. The folder has its own `CONTEXT.md`, and the root `CONTEXT.md` names it. The line `/content/` in `.gitignore` stays as it is, and no line ignores `data_fixture/`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `data_fixture/` with its `CONTEXT.md` and one folder for each of the three people.
- [ ] Write the files of Alice Example, Bob Example, and Carol Example, as the section "What the data fixture holds" says.
- [ ] Add a test that checks the data fixture: every file passes the validators, every relative link resolves, every artifact revision is correct, every state of every record type appears at least once, and each person sees only the own files.
- [ ] Make `pnpm dev` copy the data fixture into an empty or missing `content/`, and add the command that resets `content/`.
- [ ] Make the three copies of `RunningTestServer` copy the data fixture into the temporary content folder.
- [ ] Move the tests that are listed above from inline records to the data fixture.
- [ ] Update `README.md`, the root `CONTEXT.md`, and the `CONTEXT.md` of each folder that changes.

## Decisions to confirm

1. The folder name and place: `data_fixture/` at the root. Recommended, because the root already holds `content/` and `scripts/`.
2. Fixed dates or dates that move with the current day. Recommended: fixed dates, because the tests stay the same on every day. After some weeks, the development application shows every dated task as late. That is an acceptable result, because the late state is one of the states to show.
3. Whether the development application should also create permissions and shares at start, through the server. Recommended: no, in this issue.

## Done when

- On a clean clone, `pnpm install` and then `pnpm dev` give a website where Alice Example sees customers, projects, tasks, decisions, deliveries, and personal files in every view, and Carol Example sees every empty state.
- `pnpm test` passes, and the tests that are listed above read the data fixture.
- No command and no test changes a file in `data_fixture/`.

issues.title: Separate the development application from the installed application, as Heidrun does
issues.body:
Related: the data fixture of [issue #86](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/86) fills the development application only, and never the installed application.

## Problem

The repository documents one way to run Heidrun Notebook: `pnpm dev`, from a checkout. The developer cannot use Heidrun Notebook for daily work while the developer changes the code of Heidrun Notebook, because every restart, test, and experiment can reach the real notes. Today these resources have only one place each:

- The credential file of the command line tool is `~/.config/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/credential.json`. The file holds one `serverAddress` and one token, so a `login` to a second server replaces the credential of the first server.
- The content folder is `./content`, and the ports are 3100 (server) and 5173 (website). The Issue Fix Workflow in `AGENTS.md` already moves a worktree to port 3200 by hand.
- The file `.env` is the only configuration. A program that is started for daily work must never read the `.env` file of the folder that started the program.
- The authentication fixture is "for development and testing only" and its passwords are in clear text ([README.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/README.md)).
- The command line tool creates, updates, and deletes files. A coding agent that runs the tool in a terminal where `.env` or the credential file points to the daily server changes the real notes.

## How Heidrun separates the two applications

Heidrun already solved this problem with two applications, Heidrun (installed) and Heidrun Development (built from the checkout being tested). The sources are [issue 640](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/issues/640) and its [commit](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/commit/412878e5386d12dd2df792b3f3a8ee059a34c097), [issue 691](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/issues/691), [issue 769](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/issues/769), the document [application_installations.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/blob/main/docs/architecture/application_installations.md), and the code [application_profile.rs](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/blob/main/packages/apps/desktop_tauri/src/application_profile.rs). The approach has seven parts:

1. **Two identities.** The identifier is `dev.heidrun-org.heidrun` for the installed application and `dev.heidrun-org.heidrun.development` for the development application. The development window title and the application name say "Heidrun Development".
2. **The identity is chosen once, at the start, from a fixed value.** It comes from the compiled application identifier. A build option such as optimisation never changes it, and no inherited variable changes it.
3. **Separate resources.** Data folder: `~/.config/heidrun` and `~/.config/heidrun-development`. Frontend port: 1420 and 1640. Mobile access port: 47823 and 47824. Terminal session: `heidrun` and `heidrun_development`. Saved settings and window position: separate folders, one for each identifier.
4. **A guard against mixing.** The development data folder must be an absolute path and must differ from the installed data folder, also through `..` and through a symbolic link. Startup stops with an error otherwise.
5. **Inherited environment is ignored in development.** A development command often starts inside a daily-work terminal. Heidrun Development removes the inherited variables that name daily resources. Only Heidrun Development reads the `.env` file; the installed application never does.
6. **The identity is visible.** Startup prints the identifier, the data folder, the session, and the socket. The window title and the menu entry name the application.
7. **Rules, tests, and documentation.**
   - Tests prove the distinct identities, the guard (also through a symbolic link), the isolation from the inherited environment (in a child process), and the visible name.
   - `AGENTS.md` forbids a coding agent to select, launch, or control the installed application, requires a check of the target before any interaction, and says to stop when the target is uncertain.
   - One document owns the table of resources, and `README_DEV.md` links to it.
   - Shared resources are named on purpose: repository files and coding agent accounts stay shared.

## Proposal for Heidrun Notebook

Use the same seven parts. The names follow Heidrun: the installed application is "Heidrun Notebook", and the development application is "Heidrun Notebook Development". Always write both names in full.

| Resource | Heidrun Notebook (installed) | Heidrun Notebook Development |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Started by | A new start command that does not read `.env` | `pnpm dev`, as today |
| Content folder | A folder outside the checkout, for example `~/.config/heidrun_notebook/content` | `./content` of the checkout or of the temporary worktree, as today, filled from the data fixture of issue #86 |
| Server port and website port | Two new ports, different from 3100, 3200, and 5173 | 3100 and 5173, as today |
| Credential file of the command line tool | `~/.config/heidrun_notebook_ctrl/credential.json` | A different file, for example `~/.config/heidrun_notebook_ctrl_development/credential.json` |
| Name shown | "Heidrun Notebook" in the page title and in the website header | "Heidrun Notebook Development" in the page title and in the website header |
| Sessions, shares, and device logins | In the memory of the installed server | In the memory of the development server |

Details:

- The development ports stay as they are. The launch command in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.env.example`, and the tests all use them, and no installed application exists yet whose numbers must stay. The installed application gets the new ports.
- The server and the command line tool choose the identity once, at the start. An inherited environment variable cannot change it.
- The server in development stops with an error when its content folder resolves, through `..` or a symbolic link, to the installed content folder. The command line tool in development stops with an error when its credential file or its server address names the installed application.
- The credential file records the identity of the application that issued the token. The commands `auth status` and `login` print that identity, so a developer or a coding agent sees which application the command line tool talks to before any file is changed.
- The server prints its identity, content folder, port, and credential file name at start.
- The data fixture of issue #86 is copied into the development content folder only. No command copies it into the installed content folder.
- A new document owns the table of resources and the shared resources. `README.md` links to it.
- `AGENTS.md` gets a section, like the one that [issue 769](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun/issues/769) added to Heidrun: a coding agent uses the command line tool only against Heidrun Notebook Development, checks the server address and the credential file first, never runs `login` against the installed server, and stops when the target is uncertain.

## Decisions to confirm

1. **How the installed application runs.** Today the website runs in the Vite development server and the server runs with `tsx watch`. The installed application needs a build of the website and a start command without `tsx watch`. Recommended: the server serves the built website, so the installed application is one process on one port.
2. **Authentication of the installed application.** The authentication fixture has clear text passwords and is only for development. Recommended: keep it in both applications for now, with the server on `127.0.0.1` only as today, and open a separate issue for real authentication.
3. **The default installed content folder and the two new ports.** Recommended: `~/.config/heidrun_notebook/content`, with the ports chosen when the fix is made.
4. **Where the document goes.** Recommended: `docs/application_installations.md`, linked from `README.md`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add the identity for the two applications to the server and to the command line tool, chosen once at the start.
- [ ] Add the start command of the installed application, and the build of the website that it needs.
- [ ] Separate the content folder, the ports, and the credential file, as the table shows.
- [ ] Add the guards: the content folder and the credential file of the development application cannot name the installed application, also through `..` or a symbolic link.
- [ ] Make the installed application ignore `.env`, and make the development application ignore the inherited variables that name installed resources.
- [ ] Print the identity at the start, in `auth status`, and in `login`, and show the name in the page title and in the website header.
- [ ] Add tests: distinct identities, the guards, the isolation from the inherited environment, and one end-to-end test that runs both applications at the same time, writes a file through one, and proves that the other does not change.
- [ ] Write the document of the resources, add the section to `AGENTS.md`, and update `README.md`, `.env.example`, and the `CONTEXT.md` files that change.

## Done when

- The installed application and the development application run at the same time on one computer, with different ports, content folders, and credential files.
- A change, a restart, or a test of the development application never reads or changes a file of the installed application.
- `login`, `auth status`, and the website each show which application they use.
- `pnpm test` passes with the new tests.

issues.title: Add an optional comment and an optional author to every write command of heidrun_notebook_ctrl
issues.body:
## Problem

The summary of a history entry holds only the operation identifier and the paths, for example `Notebook operation eric-defiez-contact-1: customers/eric_defiez/index.md`. A person who reads the history cannot see why the change was made, and cannot see who or what made the change. This matters most when the document is shared with other people.

## Wanted

Every write command accepts an optional comment and an optional author. The history entry stores both, and the command `history` shows both.

The history entry already has the field `actor` (see [notebook_history.ts](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/packages/web_server/src/content/notebook_history.ts)), which is the authenticated person. The new field `author` names who or what wrote the change on behalf of that person, for example the coding agent.

## Tasks

- Add the option `--comment <text>` and the option `--author <name>` to the commands `create`, `update`, `patch`, and `delete`.
- For the command `apply`, add the optional fields `comment` and `author` at the top level of the operation file. One comment and one author cover the whole group of changes.
- The command line tool writes the prefix `[heidrun_notebook_ctrl] ` before the text of every comment, so a reader sees that the comment came from the command line tool.
- The server stores the comment and the author in the history entry, and the command `history` returns them in the fields `comment` and `author`. The field `actor` does not change.
- The server refuses a retry with the same operation identifier and a different comment or a different author, as it refuses any other different content.
- Show the comment and the author in the history view of the website.
- Update the skill `heidrun_notebook_ctrl`, so the coding agent writes a comment from the conversation, and gives its own name as the author, with every write.
- Add tests for each of the five commands, and for a history entry without a comment and without an author.

## Open questions

- What is the maximum length of a comment, and of an author?
- The author is free text that the caller chooses, so the server does not verify it. Is this acceptable, because the field `actor` already holds the verified person?

issues.title: Add a script that builds a container image to host Heidrun Notebook, and document it
issues.body:
## Goal

A person must be able to host Heidrun Notebook on their own machine or server with one script that builds a container image, and with one documented command that runs it. The person needs no knowledge of the repository, of pnpm, or of the development setup.

## What exists today

- The only documented way to run the product is `pnpm dev`, in [README.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/README.md). It starts the server and the Vite development server of the website together.
- The server in [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/packages/web_server/CONTEXT.md) does not serve the files of the built website. Only the Vite development server of the website sends the requests for `/api` and `/raw` to the server.
- All configuration is in environment variables, listed in [.env.example](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/.env.example).
- The files in the content folder are the source of truth. The folder `.search_index/` inside it is a copy that a person can delete at any time.
- The server needs Node.js 22.13.0 or newer, and it uses `node:sqlite`.

## The assumption that can block this work

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only, and it answers 403 when the `Host` header is not `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`. Inside a container, a person outside the container cannot reach `127.0.0.1`. The sign in also uses the authentication fixture, whose passwords are in clear text, and it sends the password over an unencrypted connection. Before the container work starts, the smallest live test is to start the server in a container, publish its port, and open the website from the host. The result of this test decides how much of the server must change. The same two facts are in this issue:

- https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/issues/121

## Work to do

1. Write one script in `scripts/` that builds the container image from a clean clone. The image holds the built website, the server, and Node.js, and it has no development dependencies.
2. Make the container serve the website and the application programming interface on one port, so the person opens one address.
3. Keep the content folder outside the image, as a volume, so the files of the people survive an update of the image.
4. Read the configuration from the environment variables of [.env.example](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/.env.example), and document each variable that a container needs.
5. Decide how the container is reachable from outside (the listening address and the `Host` header rule), and write the reason in the CONTEXT.md file of the server package.
6. Write the documentation for a person who hosts the product: the build command, the run command, the volume, the port, the variables, how to update, and how to back up the content folder.
7. Add a test that builds the image and checks that the website and the application programming interface answer from outside the container.

## Questions for the developer

- Which container tool must the script support: Docker only, or also Podman?
- Which sign in must a self-hosted container use? The authentication fixture is for development and testing only, so a real sign in may be a separate issue that this one depends on.
- Must the image be published to a registry such as GitHub Container Registry, or only built by the person who hosts the product?

## Acceptance conditions

- One command builds the image from a clean clone, and one command runs it.
- The person opens one address in a browser and sees the website.
- The content survives a stop, a removal, and a new start of the container.
- The documentation lets a person who has only Docker host the product without reading the source code.

issues.title: Add a Kanban view to the project overview
issues.body:
## Goal

Add a Kanban view to the website, so a person sees the tasks of a project as cards in columns, one column for each task status. This is an experiment: build the smallest useful version, use it on a real project, and then decide what to keep.

## Why

The tasks already carry a `status`. Today the project overview shows only a work list and a monthly calendar, so a person cannot see at one glance how much work is planned, in progress, blocked, and done. The task contract is in [task.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/product_design/concepts/task.md), and the existing website views are in [website_views.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/docs/product_design/website_views.md).

## Proposal

- Each project overview offers a Kanban view next to the work list and the monthly calendar.
- The view has one column for each of these task statuses: `planned`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, and `done`.
- Each card is one task. A card shows the title, the person in `assigned_to`, the date in `due_on`, and the reason in `blocked_reason` for a blocked task.
- The view includes the tasks of the subprojects, and each card shows which project holds the task, as the work list does.
- The view reads the same task records as the work list and the calendar. It stores nothing new.
- The view is read-only, like every other view of the website. A person changes the status by asking the coding agent, which writes the task with `heidrun_notebook_ctrl`.

## Open questions

- Do the statuses `proposed`, `rejected`, and `cancelled` get a column, or do they stay outside the board, as the work list keeps them outside the delivery work?
- Does the view show the filters of the work list (responsible person, blockers, overdue work)?
- Does a card open the task document when a person selects it?

## Out of scope

- Moving a card with the mouse. The website has no write operation.
- Limits on the number of cards in a column.

## Acceptance conditions

- A project with tasks in several statuses shows each task in the column of its status.
- A task of a subproject shows in the Kanban view of the parent project, with the name of its own project.
- A task with a status that has no column does not disappear without a trace: the view tells the person where to find it.
- The view has a test in the end-to-end layer of the package `web_frontend`.

issues.title: Keep a language model wiki in Heidrun Notebook with mnemo_wiki
issues.body:
## Goal

Use [mnemo_wiki](https://github.com/jeromeetienne/mnemo_wiki) to keep a language model wiki inside Heidrun Notebook. A language model wiki is the idea that Andrej Karpathy describes in [his note](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f): the coding agent reads sources and writes linked markdown pages, instead of keeping the knowledge in a chat history.

## Why mnemo_wiki fits Heidrun Notebook

- mnemo_wiki stores the wiki as markdown files with front matter, in the Open Knowledge Format.
- Heidrun Notebook also keeps markdown files with front matter in `content/` as the source of truth (see [CONTEXT.md](https://github.com/heidrun-org/heidrun_notebook/blob/main/CONTEXT.md)).
- mnemo_wiki never calls a language model itself. Claude Code writes the pages and follows the `CLAUDE.md` file inside the wiki.

## Plan

1. Put one mnemo_wiki wiki in a folder of Heidrun Notebook `content/`, so the website shows the wiki pages and the search finds them.
2. Let Claude Code follow the `CLAUDE.md` file of mnemo_wiki to ingest sources such as meeting notes and customer documents, and to write the summary pages, the entity pages, and the concept pages.
3. Run `npx mnemo_wiki validate` and `npx mnemo_wiki lint` to check the links, the orphan pages, and the front matter.
